hints: Focus on what happens to nuclear charge and atomic size as you move left to right across Period 3 from Na to Cl.
Remember that $Na_2O$ and $MgO$ are strongly basic, while $Al_2O_3$ in the middle can react with both acids and bases.
Link increasing non-metallic character across the period to both stronger pull on electrons and more acidic oxides like $SO_2$ and $P_4O_{10}$.
walkthrough:
**Trend in electronegativity across Period 3**

Think of going from Na to Cl. Protons are added to the nucleus, but electrons go into the same shell, so shielding stays similar.

This means effective nuclear charge increases and atoms get smaller, so the pull on bonding electrons gets stronger:
$$\text{electronegativity increases from Na to Cl}$$

**Trend in acid-base behaviour of the oxides**

Start on the left with metals. $Na_2O$ and $MgO$ react with acids to form salts and water, so they are basic.

In the middle, $Al_2O_3$ reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric.

**Finish the sequence on the right**

Move to the non-metals on the right. $SiO_2$, $P_4O_{10}$, $SO_2$ and $SO_3$ react with bases to form salts, so they are acidic.

Putting it together gives:
$$\text{basic} \rightarrow \text{amphoteric} \rightarrow \text{acidic}$$

**Choose the correct row**

We need increases for electronegativity and basic to amphoteric to acidic for the oxides.

That combination matches only one row.

options.A: The oxide trend is correct, basic to amphoteric to acidic, but electronegativity does not decrease. Across a period nuclear charge rises with similar shielding, so electronegativity increases from Na to Cl.
options.B: Both parts are reversed. Electronegativity increases, not decreases, and oxides go from basic on the left ($Na_2O$, $MgO$) to acidic on the right ($P_4O_{10}$, $SO_2$), not the other way round.
options.C: This is correct. Electronegativity increases across Period 3 due to increasing nuclear charge. Oxides change from basic ($Na_2O$, $MgO$) through amphoteric ($Al_2O_3$) to acidic ($SiO_2$, $P_4O_{10}$, $SO_2$).
options.D: Electronegativity increasing is correct, but the oxide trend is backwards. Students who confuse Group trends or think non-metal oxides are basic may pick this. In fact metal oxides on the left are basic and non-metal oxides on the right are acidic.
